description: Crafted Datadog corpus for the incident question set (questions.json). Objects have the shape of Datadog API responses so the real adapters parse them. Services: checkout, checkout-worker (similar name), payments, auth-api, sökmotor, inventory, orders, recommendations, ledger, orders-db, fulfillment, notifications, billing, edge-gateway, checkout-api, storefront; environments prod and staging. 'logBursts' are runs of near-identical logs that the harness expands into individual logs (support/datadog.rs, expand_burst). Dashboards are full dashboard definitions (the fake list endpoint returns only the summary keys; GET /api/v1/dashboard/{id} returns the rest). 'incidentTimelines' and 'incidentAttachments' (per incident ID) and 'notebooks' are served by the per-incident timeline, attachments and notebook endpoints. The questions are asked at 2026-03-12T09:00:00Z in Europe/Stockholm, so 'yesterday' is 2026-03-10T23:00:00Z..2026-03-11T23:00:00Z. The recorded fixtures' monitors, dashboards, SLOs and metrics are indexed alongside as unrelated distractors. Checkout logs in January and February belong to q20-q23, which set their own 'now'.

monitors.name: Ledger reconciliation drift
monitors.message: Runbook RB-LED-3. This alert fires when the nightly balance comparison between the accounting database and the payment provider settlement files disagrees by more than 100 entries. First, open the Finance Operations dashboard and confirm which settlement batch is affected; the batch identifier is printed in the alert context. Second, check whether the settlement file for that batch arrived on time: files are delivered to the sftp inbox between 01:00 and 02:30 UTC, and a late file is the most common cause of a transient mismatch that resolves itself on the next comparison. Third, look at the export job history in the scheduler; a failed or partially completed export leaves the comparison with missing rows, which shows up as a sudden jump in the mismatch counter rather than a slow increase. If the export failed, rerun it from the scheduler with the same batch identifier and wait for the comparison to finish before paging anyone else. Fourth, if the settlement file and the export are both complete, compare the currency breakdown: a mismatch concentrated in one currency usually means a rate table was not refreshed, and the treasury team owns that table. Fifth, confirm that no manual adjustments were booked during the comparison window; manual bookings are listed in the adjustments report and must be approved by two people from the finance team. Do not delete or edit booked entries to make the numbers match: every correction is a new compensating entry with a reference to the incident. Keep the incident channel updated every thirty minutes with the current mismatch count, the suspected cause and the next action, and hand over explicitly at the end of your shift. Escalate to the accounting platform on-call engineer when the mismatch keeps growing for more than one hour or when more than one settlement batch is affected at the same time. Replica lag: the comparison reads from the postgres read replica, so replica lag makes recent bookings invisible and inflates the mismatch. Check the replica lag panel; if it is above five minutes, pause the comparison, wait until the replica has caught up and rerun it instead of correcting entries.

root_cause.value: Root cause of the checkout outage: a connection leak in the promo-code lookup (released on 20 February) never returned connections, so the checkout database pool ran dry.

resolution.value: Disabled the promo-code lookup with a feature flag and restarted the checkout pods.

definition.text:
# What happened
The intermediate certificate presented by the bank gateway expired at 08:14 UTC, so every TLS handshake from payments failed and card payments were declined.

# Action items
- Automate renewal of the expired certificate bundle.
- Alert 30 days before any certificate in the trust store expires.
- Add a synthetic test that exercises the full TLS chain.
